solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply x by both terms of the second bracket.
Multiply 3 by both terms of the second bracket.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply each term of the first bracket by each term of the second, then combine the x-terms.

whyThisWorks.value: The distributive law lets a bracket be multiplied term by term, so (x + 3)(x + 5) splits into x(x + 5) plus 3(x + 5). Adding those two partial products and combining like terms gives the quadratic. The middle coefficient 8 is 3 + 5 and the constant 15 is 3 × 5, which is exactly why factorising a quadratic asks for two numbers that add and multiply to those values.

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying only the matching positions to get x² + 15.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Multiplying only the matching positions to get x² + 15.

commonErrors.misconception: Getting 8x² instead of 8x by mishandling the letters.

examTip.value: Set the work out in two lines — x(x + 5) then 3(x + 5) — instead of trying to do all four products at once. It is slower to write but far harder to get wrong.
